question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: **Tread on your toes**
solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Offend or annoy someone .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom "**Tread on your toes**" means to offend or annoy someone, especially by interfering in their responsibilities or personal matters.
 
• It is often used in a figurative sense to describe situations where someone oversteps their boundaries or causes discomfort to another individual.
 
• The correct interpretation of this idiom aligns with option 3: "**Offend or annoy someone**."

Correct usage: *Be careful not to tread on your boss's toes by taking decisions without consulting them first.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Similar Idioms:**
 
 
• **Step on someone's toes:** To offend or upset someone by encroaching on their authority or responsibilities.
 
• **Rub someone the wrong way:** To irritate or annoy someone, often unintentionally.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Usage:**
 
 
• She doesn't want to tread on anyone's toes, so she avoids discussing sensitive topics.
 
• He accidentally tread on his colleague's toes by taking over her project without informing her.
